title_en: Regulations on the Administration of Protection of Underwater Cultural Relics of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in order to strengthen the administration of the protection of underwater cultural relics, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics.

Article 3 The underwater cultural relics specified in Items (1) and (2) of the first paragraph of Article 2 of these Regulations are owned by the State, and the State shall exercise jurisdiction over them. For the underwater cultural relics specified in Item (3) of the first paragraph of Article 2 of these Regulations, which are cultural relics of unknown origin remaining in other jurisdictional sea areas beyond foreign territorial seas and in the high seas, the State shall have the right to identify their owners.

Article 4 The competent department of cultural relics under the State Council shall be responsible for the protection of underwater cultural relics nationwide. The competent departments of cultural relics of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the protection of underwater cultural relics within their administrative regions.
Other relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the protection of underwater cultural relics.
Underwater cultural relics in other sea areas beyond China's territorial sea that are under China's jurisdiction in accordance with Chinese law shall be protected by the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council.

Article 5 Any unit or individual shall have the obligation to protect underwater cultural relics in accordance with the law.
People's governments at all levels shall attach importance to the protection of underwater cultural relics, properly handle the relationship between economic and social development and the protection of underwater cultural relics, and ensure the safety of underwater cultural relics.

Article 6 Based on the value of underwater cultural relics, the people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, verify and announce the designation of cultural relic protection units, and register and announce immovable cultural relics that have not been designated as cultural relic protection units.
The competent departments of cultural relics of local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in light of the protection needs of different cultural relics, formulate specific protection measures for cultural relic protection units and immovable cultural relics that have not been designated as cultural relic protection units, and announce such measures for implementation.

Article 7 The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may delineate and announce waters where underwater cultural relics are relatively concentrated and require overall protection as underwater cultural relic protection zones, and may adjust such zones based on actual circumstances. Where an underwater cultural relic protection zone involves two or more provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, or involves other sea areas beyond China's territorial sea that are under China's jurisdiction in accordance with Chinese law, the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council shall delineate and adjust such zone, and shall submit it to the State Council for verification and announcement.
When delineating or adjusting an underwater cultural relic protection zone, opinions from relevant departments and water area use right holders shall be sought, and opinions from experts and the public shall be heard; where a military administration zone or military sea area is involved, opinions from relevant military organs shall also be sought.
The unit that delineates or adjusts an underwater cultural relic protection zone shall formulate a protection plan. The competent department of cultural relics under the State Council or the competent department of cultural relics of the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall, based on the protection plan, clearly mark the scope and boundaries of the underwater cultural relic protection zone, formulate specific protection measures, and announce them for implementation.
Within an underwater cultural relic protection zone, activities such as fishing and blasting that endanger the safety of underwater cultural relics shall be prohibited.

Article 8 Acts such as destroying, illegally salvaging, looting, illegally distributing, concealing, trafficking, or smuggling underwater cultural relics are strictly prohibited.
Where activities such as scientific research, resource exploration and exploitation, tourism, diving, fishing, aquaculture, sand extraction, sewage discharge, or waste dumping are carried out in waters under China's jurisdiction, the relevant laws and regulations shall be complied with, and the safety of underwater cultural relics shall not be endangered.

Article 9 Any unit or individual that discovers underwater cultural relics suspected to be those specified in Items (1) and (2) of the first paragraph of Article 2 of these Regulations by any means shall promptly report to the competent department of cultural relics of the local people's government at the place where the discovery is made or at a nearby location, and shall hand over any cultural relics that have already been salvaged from the water.
Upon receiving the report, the competent department of cultural relics shall, unless under special circumstances, arrive at the scene within 24 hours, immediately take measures for protection, and propose a handling opinion within 7 days. Where it is found that the underwater cultural relics have been moved or have suffered actual damage, rescue protection shall be carried out and detailed records shall be made. Cultural relics that have been salvaged from the water shall be promptly registered, catalogued, and properly kept.
The competent department of cultural relics shall protect the site where the underwater cultural relics were discovered, and may, when necessary, work together with the public security organ or the maritime law enforcement agency to carry out protection work, and shall report the protection work to the people's government at the same level and to the competent department of cultural relics of the people's government at the next higher level. Where important cultural relics are discovered, a report shall be submitted level by level to the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council, which shall propose a handling opinion within 15 days after receiving the report.

Article 10 Any unit or individual that discovers underwater cultural relics suspected to be those specified in Item (3) of the first paragraph of Article 2 of these Regulations by any means shall promptly report to the competent department of cultural relics of the local people's government at a nearby location, or directly report to the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council. The competent department of cultural relics of the local people's government that receives the report shall report level by level to the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council. The competent department of cultural relics under the State Council shall promptly propose a handling opinion and report it to the State Council.

Article 11 Archaeological investigations, surveys, and excavations of underwater cultural relics in waters under China's jurisdiction shall be carried out by units qualified for archaeological excavation, which shall submit an application to the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council. The application materials shall include a work plan and a certificate of archaeological excavation qualification. Where the proposed archaeological investigation, survey, or excavation activity is to be carried out in China's internal waters or territorial sea, an opinion issued by the competent department of cultural relics of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the activity is located shall also be provided.
The competent department of cultural relics under the State Council shall, within 30 days from the date of receiving the application materials, make a decision on whether to grant permission. If permission is granted, it shall issue an approval document; if permission is not granted, it shall inform the applicant in writing and state the reasons.
Before making a decision, the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council shall seek opinions from relevant scientific research institutions and experts. Where a military administration zone or military sea area is involved, opinions from relevant military organs shall also be sought. Where the proposed activity involves archaeological investigations, surveys, or excavations of underwater cultural relics in other sea areas beyond China's territorial sea that are under China's jurisdiction in accordance with Chinese law, the approval of the State Council shall be obtained.

Article 12 Any foreign organization or international organization that conducts archaeological investigations, surveys, or excavations of underwater cultural relics in waters under China's jurisdiction shall do so through cooperation with a Chinese entity and shall obtain permission. The Chinese entity shall have the qualification for archaeological excavation; the foreign entity shall be a specialized archaeological research institution with experts engaged in research in the relevant or similar field and with certain practical archaeological work experience.
Where underwater cultural relic archaeological investigations, surveys, or excavations are carried out through Sino-foreign cooperation, the Chinese entity shall submit an application to the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council. The application materials shall include a letter of intent for cooperation between the Chinese and foreign entities, a work plan, and relevant materials demonstrating that both cooperating parties meet the requirements of the preceding paragraph. Where the proposed archaeological investigation, survey, or excavation activity is to be carried out in China's internal waters or territorial sea, an opinion issued by the competent department of cultural relics of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the activity is located shall also be provided.
After receiving the application materials, the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council shall seek opinions from relevant scientific research institutions and experts. Where a military administration zone or military sea area is involved, opinions from relevant military organs shall also be sought. The application materials shall be submitted to the relevant departments for review in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State. If the review is passed, a special permission from the State Council shall be requested; if the review fails, the applicant shall be informed in writing and the reasons shall be stated.
The underwater cultural relics, natural specimens, and original data from archaeological records obtained through Sino-foreign cooperative archaeological investigations, surveys, or excavations shall all belong to China.

Article 13 Where a large-scale capital construction project is to be carried out in waters under China's jurisdiction, the construction entity shall, in advance, request the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council or the competent department of cultural relics of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government to organize archaeological investigations and surveys in the areas within the scope of the project where cultural relics may be buried. If archaeological excavation is necessary, the approval procedures shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics.

Article 14 Archaeological investigations, surveys, and excavations of underwater cultural relics in waters under China's jurisdiction shall be conducted for the purposes of cultural relic protection and scientific research, and shall comply with relevant laws and regulations, subject to the management of the competent authorities.
After the completion of archaeological investigations, surveys, or excavations, the unit that conducted such activities shall submit to the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council and the competent department of cultural relics of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government a completion report, an archaeological excavation report, pictures of the physical objects obtained, copies of relevant materials, and the like.
All underwater cultural relics recovered during archaeological investigations, surveys, or excavations shall be promptly registered, catalogued, and properly kept. They shall be transferred in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State to state-owned museums, libraries, or other state-owned cultural relic collecting institutions designated by the competent department of cultural relics under the State Council or the competent department of cultural relics of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for collection.
Where archaeological investigations, surveys, or excavations are conducted through Sino-foreign cooperation, the Chinese entity shall submit the physical objects and materials specified in the preceding two paragraphs.

Article 15 Conducting archaeological investigations, surveys, excavations, or similar activities of underwater cultural relics without approval is strictly prohibited.
Any individual conducting archaeological investigations, surveys, excavations, or similar activities of underwater cultural relics in any form is strictly prohibited.

Article 16 The competent departments of cultural relics, cultural relic collecting institutions, and the like shall, through means such as holding exhibitions, opening to visitors, and conducting scientific research, give full play to the role of underwater cultural relics, strengthen the publicity and education of fine traditional Chinese culture, the legal system for the protection of underwater cultural relics, and the like, and enhance the public's awareness of the protection of underwater cultural relics and the public's enthusiasm for participating in the protection of underwater cultural relics.

Article 17 The competent departments of cultural relics, public security organs, and maritime law enforcement agencies shall carry out law enforcement work for the protection of underwater cultural relics according to their respective functions and duties, and shall strengthen law enforcement coordination.
The competent departments of cultural relics of the people's governments at or above the county level shall enhance communication and coordination with relevant departments in the protection of underwater cultural relics, and share information on law enforcement concerning underwater cultural relics.

Article 18 Any unit or individual shall have the right to report to the competent department of cultural relics any act that violates the provisions of these Regulations and endangers the safety of underwater cultural relics. The competent department of cultural relics shall establish a reporting channel and make it available to the public, and shall handle the relevant reports promptly in accordance with the law.

Article 19 Those who make outstanding contributions to the protection of underwater cultural relics shall be given spiritual encouragement or material rewards in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 20 Where staff members of the competent departments of cultural relics and other relevant departments abuse their powers, neglect their duties, or engage in malpractice for personal gain in the protection of underwater cultural relics, the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions in accordance with the law; where a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with the law.

Article 21 Where construction projects or operations such as blasting, drilling, or excavation are carried out without authorization within the protection zones of cultural relic protection units, legal liability shall be investigated in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics.
Article 23 These Regulations shall come into force as of April 1, 2022.
